answer: Per-person token budget: a verifier checks a person once, then each epoch blind-signs 20 tokens for them. Every answer or grade must spend one token, and validators reject any token serial already spent. Splitting into ten agents gains nothing: they still share the same 20 tokens, so extra identities add upkeep but no extra actions. Like a relic of wartime ration books, it rests on the issuer: a careless or bribed verifier collapses the scheme like timber laid over a karst sinkhole, so issuers need audits and revocation.
